# text-to-image

Imported as `@elffuss/ai/text-to-image`, `@elffuss/ai/text-to-image/sizes`.

## `sdk/text-to-image/impl.js`

The text-to-image task where the model runs (a Worker): SANA-Sprint 0.6B with ONNX Runtime Web on WebGPU. Three sessions (the Gemma 2 text model with 4-bit weights, the transformer and the decoder in float16), the 4-bit token table and the tokenizer, all from the store through the task context and checked against the registry. The model's numbers (latent channels, scaling factor, guidance scale, sampler) are read from its own configuration files at the pinned commit. No fetch, no DOM.

### `GUIDANCE_SCALE`

The guidance value the distilled model was made for (the pipeline's default).

## `sdk/text-to-image/index.js`

@elffuss/ai/text-to-image: pictures from a text, in the browser. SANA-Sprint 0.6B (NVlabs, Apache-2.0), with its Gemma 2 text model, on WebGPU with ONNX Runtime Web; the model comes through the Elffuss model store at a pinned revision. One to four steps; the same prompt, seed, steps and size give the same picture, the one the reference pipeline (diffusers) gives for them.

### Type `ImageRequest`

```ts
import('./request.js').ImageRequest
```

```ts
{ blob: Blob, mime: 'image/png', width: number, height: number, seed: number, steps: number, prompt: string, aspect: string|null, model: string, device: 'webgpu', promptTokens: number, truncated: boolean }
```

What `generate()` gives: the picture as a PNG `blob` and everything needed to make it again (`seed`, `steps`, `prompt`, `aspect` or `width` × `height`). `truncated`: the prompt was longer than the 300 tokens the model reads.

## `sdk/text-to-image/pipeline.js`

One picture from a prompt, given the three models as functions (so that this file runs the same in a Worker, on a page or in Node's tests with stand-ins): It reports each stage (encode, step i of n, decode) and stops between models when the signal is aborted.

### Type `Models`

```ts
{ encode: (text: string) => number[], embed: (ids: number[]) => Float32Array, hidden: number, runEncoder: (embeds: Float32Array, tokens: number) => Promise<Float32Array>, runTransformer: (o: { latents: Float32Array, h: number, w: number, caption: Float32Array, tokens: number, time: number, guidance: number }) => Promise<Float32Array>, runDecoder: (latents: Float32Array, h: number, w: number) => Promise<{ data: Float32Array, height: number, width: number }>, config: { channels: number, factor: number, scaling: number, guidance: number, sigmaData?: number } }
```

`config` comes from the model's own configuration files: latent channels, the decoder's spatial factor, its scaling factor, and the guidance value the transformer is given (4.5 × guidance_embeds_scale).

## `sdk/text-to-image/pixels.js`

From the decoder's output to pixels, as the reference pipeline does it: an image of three planes in [-1, 1] (channels first), scaled and centre-cropped to the asked size when it differs from the generated one (bilinear, corners not aligned, like torch's interpolate), then mapped to 0-255 with rounding.

## `sdk/text-to-image/prompt.js`

How SANA-Sprint reads a prompt, as diffusers' SanaSprintPipeline does: the prompt is lowercased and trimmed and put after a fixed instruction for the text model (the "complex human instruction" of the pipeline, written below as the pipeline has it), and the text model reads the whole text. The transformer is then given the first token's state and the states of the last 299 positions of the text padded to the instruction's length plus 298: in practice the prompt's own tokens. Padding positions carry no weight (the pipeline masks them out), so they are left out here instead of being computed.

### `INSTRUCTION`

The instruction the pipeline puts before every prompt, line by line.

### `MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS`

The longest prompt the model reads, in tokens (the pipeline's max_sequence_length).

### `normalizePrompt(prompt)`

The prompt as the pipeline reads it: lowercased and trimmed.

### `captionTokens(encode, prompt)`

The tokens the text model reads and which of its output states the transformer
is given.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `encode` | `(text: string) => number[]` | the Gemma tokenizer, with the beginning-of-text token first (as `add_special_tokens` gives it) |
| `prompt` | `string` |  |

Returns `{ ids: number[], keep: number[], promptTokens: number, truncated: boolean }`: `ids`: the tokens to run (instruction and prompt, never padding); `keep`: the positions of `ids` whose states go to the transformer, in order; `promptTokens`: how many of the prompt's tokens it sees; `truncated`: the prompt was longer than the model reads and its end was cut

## `sdk/text-to-image/request.js`

What a caller may ask for, checked and completed in one place: on the page before anything is sent to the Worker, and again in the Worker. A request is plain JSON, so a chat's tool call `{"tool": "image.generate", "args": {...}}` is passed as it is.

### `DEFAULT_STEPS`

The number of steps when none is asked: the two-step schedule the model was distilled for.

### `MAX_PROMPT_CHARS`

Longest prompt accepted, in characters (the model reads at most 300 tokens of it).

### `DEFAULT_STRENGTH`

How far a picture made from another may move from it when none is asked (0 close … 1 free).

### `strengthTime(strength)`

The SDEdit start time of a strength (TrigFlow time, π/2 is all noise). What a picture
keeps changes fast near π/2, so the scale is even in log(tan t): t = atan(2·30^strength).
0 → 1.11 (the picture barely moves), 0.3 → 1.39 (small changes of pose and detail),
0.6 → 1.51 (a new light or style, the same layout: "at night", "as a watercolour"),
1 → 1.55 (the text leads, the picture only hints). Measured on SANA-Sprint 0.6B.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `strength` | `number` | 0 to 1 |

### `sizeFromImage(w, h)`

The size of a picture made from one of w × h: about a megapixel, its shape, multiples of 8.

Returns `{ width: number, height: number }`.

### Type `ImageRequest`

```ts
{ prompt: string, aspect?: '1:1'|'4:3'|'3:2'|'16:9'|'3:4'|'2:3'|'9:16', width?: number, height?: number, seed?: number, steps?: 1|2|3|4 }
```

`aspect` (default 1:1) picks a trained size of about a megapixel; `width` and `height` (256 to 2048) ask for an exact size instead, generated at the nearest trained shape and scaled and cropped to it. `seed` (0 to 4294967295) repeats a picture: the same prompt, seed, steps and size give the same image; without one, a random seed is used and returned. `steps` 1 to 4 (default 2). `image` (optional): a picture to start from, `{ width, height, rgba }` (RGBA bytes; TextToImage turns a Blob or an ImageBitmap into one); the result keeps its shape (about a megapixel) and `strength` (0 to 1, default 0.6) says how far it may move from it: low keeps the picture and changes its look, high follows the text more.

## `sdk/text-to-image/rng.js`

Gaussian noise drawn exactly as PyTorch draws it on the CPU, so that a seed gives here the same starting noise as the reference pipeline (diffusers with `torch.Generator('cpu').manual_seed(seed)`): the same picture for the same prompt and seed. PyTorch seeds a 32-bit Mersenne Twister (MT19937) with the seed, fills a float tensor of 16 or more values with uniforms of 24 bits, and turns them into normals in blocks of 16 with the Box-Muller transform (value j with value j + 8); a size that is not a multiple of 16 redraws the last 16. The arithmetic is done in float32 as PyTorch does (Math.fround), which matches it to the last bit or one unit in the last place.

### `class Mt19937`

A Mersenne Twister of 32 bits, seeded as PyTorch seeds its CPU generator.

- `.constructor(seed)`
- `.next()`: The next 32-bit unsigned integer.
- `.uniform()`: A uniform float in [0, 1) from 24 random bits, as PyTorch makes a float one.

### `randn(gen, n)`

`torch.randn(n, generator=g)` for a float tensor of n ≥ 16 values, from the
generator's current state (later calls continue the same sequence, as the
pipeline's noise for each step does).

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `gen` | `Mt19937` |  |
| `n` | `number` |  |

Returns `Float32Array`.

### `MAX_SEED`

The largest seed: PyTorch keeps the low 32 bits of a seed.

### `randomSeed()`

A random seed, for a picture nobody asked to repeat.

## `sdk/text-to-image/schedule.js`

The few-step sampler of SANA-Sprint (continuous-time consistency, "TrigFlow"), as diffusers' SCMScheduler and SanaSprintPipeline do it. Time runs from π/2 (pure noise) to 0 (the picture). Each step scales the latents into the model's input, turns the model's output into a velocity, takes the clean estimate x0 and, unless it is the last step, adds fresh noise for the next time. Pure functions over Float32Arrays; the arithmetic is float32 like the reference.

### `SIGMA_DATA`

The noise level of the training data (scheduler_config.json, `sigma_data`).

### `MAX_TIME`

The first time of every schedule: π/2 as the reference writes it.

### `TWO_STEP_TIME`

The middle time of the two-step schedule, the one the model was distilled for.

### `STEP_CHOICES`

Steps the model was trained to work with.

### `timesteps(steps)`

The times of a schedule of `steps` steps, from π/2 down to 0 (steps + 1 values).
Two steps use the distilled middle time 1.3; the others are evenly spaced.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `steps` | `number` | 1 to 4 |

Returns `Float32Array`.

### `sdeditTimes(t)`

The schedule of SDEdit (a picture from another picture) starting at time `t`
(π/2 is all noise): the two-step schedule scaled to start there,
[t, t·1.3/(π/2), 0], as diffusers' Sprint img2img runs with
max_timesteps = t and intermediate_timesteps = t·1.3/(π/2).

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `t` | `number` | in (0, π/2] |

Returns `Float32Array`.

### `modelInput(latents, s, sigmaData = SIGMA_DATA)`

What the transformer is given at time s: the latents scaled to its input, and
the time as it sees it (between 0 and 1).

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `latents` | `Float32Array` |  |
| `s` | `number` |  |
| `[sigmaData]` | `number` |  |

Returns `{ input: Float32Array, time: number, scale: number }`.

### `step({ latents, input, output, time, scale, s, t, noise, sigmaData = SIGMA_DATA })`

One step: from the model's output at time s to the clean estimate x0, and the
latents at the next time t (x0 itself when t is 0).

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `o` | `{ latents: Float32Array, input: Float32Array, output: Float32Array, time: number, scale: number, s: number, t: number, noise?: Float32Array, sigmaData?: number }` | `noise` is a standard normal draw of the latents' size (unused when t is 0) |

Returns `{ x0: Float32Array, next: Float32Array }`.

## `sdk/text-to-image/shapes.js`

Picture sizes. SANA-Sprint was trained on a fixed set of sizes of about a megapixel (diffusers' ASPECT_RATIO_1024_BIN, height × width); like the reference pipeline, a requested size is generated at the trained size of the nearest shape and then scaled and cropped to what was asked. The aspect presets are trained sizes, so they are generated as they are.

### `TRAINED_SIZES`

Trained sizes, keyed by height / width, as [height, width], in the reference's order.

### `ASPECTS`

The shapes offered by name (width:height), each a trained size.

### `MIN_SIDE`

Smallest and largest side a caller may ask for.

### `nearestTrained(width, height)`

The trained size nearest in shape to width × height (the reference's rule, first on a tie).

### `resolveSize({ aspect, width, height } = {})`

The size to generate at and the size to give back.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `req` | `{ aspect?: string, width?: number, height?: number }` |  |

Returns `{ width: number, height: number, genWidth: number, genHeight: number, aspect: string\|null }`.
